title: Pre-gated MoE: An Algorithm-System Co-Design for Fast and Scalable Mixture-of-Expert Inference
problem: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures suffer from high memory demands and dynamic sparse expert activation that restrict practical applicability. Offloading expert parameters to CPU memory incurs prohibitive latency overhead when migrating activated experts to GPU.
motivation: MoE is essential for scaling large language models efficiently, but current implementations are impractical due to memory constraints and performance overheads limiting real-world deployment.
method: Pre-gated MoE predicts which expert networks will be needed before processing, making expert selection predictable rather than dynamic. This lets the system transfer necessary experts from CPU storage to GPU memory in advance, rather than fetching them on-demand during computation. By coordinating algorithm design with hardware scheduling, Pre-gated MoE reduces both the total memory footprint and the latency of expert transfers.
key_novelty: Pre-gating predicts which experts will be needed before processing input, making expert selection predictable rather than dynamic—this avoids the latency cost of fetching experts on-demand.
contributions: Novel pre-gating function for reducing dynamic expert activation in MoE
Algorithm-system co-design framework for efficient MoE inference
Significant reduction in GPU memory consumption without sacrificing model quality
Enables single-GPU deployment of large-scale LLMs at scale
primary_theme: Efficient MoE inference through predictable expert scheduling
